chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
question_text: You are a Botanist working in the area of plant breeding. Describe the various steps that you will undertake to release a new variety.

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.17, printed question 5. insider_note: Five steps, and the marks follow them. List all five first — an examiner who can see the five headings will find every mark, and the list alone is worth one.

page_header: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production (Botany-II) · 8 marks

steps.label: The five steps
steps.margin_note: All five, numbered, before any explanation. Eight lines and one mark secured.
lines: Releasing a new crop variety takes FIVE steps:
1. Collection of variability
2. Evaluation and selection of parents
3. Cross hybridisation among the selected
parents
4. Selection and testing of superior
recombinants
5. Testing, release and commercialisation of
the new cultivars
steps.why: The five steps run in one order — gather, choose, cross, select, release — and every later step depends on the one before it.
common_mistakes: Naming three steps. There are FIVE, and each is a heading in the answer.
Putting selection before hybridisation. You must cross before you can select recombinants.

steps.label: Collection of variability
steps.margin_note: Two marks here. Define germplasm collection in full — it is asked as a VSAQ on its own.
lines: 1. COLLECTION OF VARIABILITY
Genetic variability is the raw material of any
breeding programme — without differences there
is nothing to select from.
Pre-existing variability is available in the
WILD RELATIVES of crop plants.
Collecting and preserving all the wild varieties
and species is a PRE-REQUISITE, because it is
the only way to exploit the natural genes in the
population.
The entire collection of plants or seeds having
all the DIVERSE ALLELES for all genes in a given
crop is called the GERM PLASM COLLECTION.
steps.why: A breeder can only recombine alleles that already exist somewhere, so the size of the germplasm collection sets the limit on what can ever be bred.
common_mistakes: Saying variability can be created at will. It is COLLECTED from wild relatives.
Leaving out germplasm collection. It is the named term and this mark is largely for it.
Saying wild relatives are useless. They carry the genes for disease resistance.
steps.memory_tip: You can only breed with alleles somebody has already collected.

steps.label: Evaluation and selection of parents
steps.margin_note: Evaluation, multiplication, and pure lines by self pollination.
lines: 2. EVALUATION AND SELECTION OF
PARENTS The germplasm is EVALUATED to identify
plants with the desired characters.
The selected plants are MULTIPLIED and used in
hybridisation.
PURE LINES are created by continuous SELF
POLLINATION, so the parents are homozygous and
of known genotype.
steps.why: A cross can only be interpreted if both parents breed true, so purifying the parents comes before any crossing.
common_mistakes: Skipping the pure lines. Self pollination to homozygosity is what this step is for.
Saying evaluation means testing the yield of hybrids. It means examining the GERMPLASM for useful characters.
steps.memory_tip: Pick them, then purify them, then cross them.

steps.label: Cross hybridisation
steps.margin_note: What is combined, an example, and both difficulties.
lines: 3. CROSS HYBRIDISATION AMONG SELECTED
PARENTS The desired characters from different parents
are combined by crossing them.
Example: a high yielding parent is crossed with
a disease resistant one.
It is very TIME CONSUMING and LABORIOUS:
each cross needs emasculation and hand pollination.
It is also uncertain — usually only ONE cross in
a few hundred gives the desired combination.
steps.why: Each cross is done by hand on individual flowers, so the low success rate translates directly into years of work.
common_mistakes: Saying hybridisation always works. Only about one in a few hundred crosses succeeds.
Leaving out the difficulty. The time and the low success rate are part of the mark.
steps.memory_tip: Hundreds of crosses for one useful combination.

steps.label: Selection and testing of recombinants
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Selection, superiority to both parents, and the homozygosity that stops segregation.
lines: 4. SELECTION AND TESTING OF SUPERIOR
RECOMBINANTS Plants with the desired combination
of characters are selected from among the hybrids.
This is the CRITICAL step, and it needs careful
scientific evaluation of the progeny.
It yields offspring SUPERIOR TO BOTH PARENTS.
The selected plants are then SELF POLLINATED for
several generations to reach HOMOZYGOSITY,
so that the characters no longer SEGREGATE in
the progeny and the variety breeds true.
steps.why: A hybrid that is still heterozygous will not breed true, so its good characters would scatter in the next generation unless homozygosity is reached first.
common_mistakes: Stopping at 'the best plants are selected'. The self pollination to homozygosity is half this mark.
Saying the offspring resemble one parent. They are SUPERIOR TO BOTH.
Leaving out segregation. Preventing it is why homozygosity is needed.
steps.memory_tip: Select the best, then make it breed true.

steps.label: Testing, release and commercialisation
steps.margin_note: Both kinds of field, the comparison, and certification before release.

lines.text: Research field, then farmer's field, then

lines: 5. TESTING, RELEASE AND
COMMERCIALISATION The newly selected lines are
evaluated for YIELD and DISEASE RESISTANCE.
They are first grown in RESEARCH FIELDS, under
controlled conditions.
The hybrid line is then tested in FARMERS'
FIELDS, in at least three different seasons and
at several locations.
The material is compared with the best available
LOCAL CULTIVAR.
Only after this evaluation and CERTIFICATION is
the variety released.
steps.why: A variety that performs well in one research plot may fail in a farmer's field, so the comparison against the best local cultivar is the real test.
common_mistakes: Releasing straight from the research field. Farmers' field trials come first.
Leaving out the comparison with the local cultivar. A new variety must BEAT what farmers already grow.
Forgetting certification. Release follows certification, not the other way round.
steps.memory_tip: It must beat what the farmer already grows, in the farmer's own field.
